title: A project's own git hook guards are lost on every fresh clone, silently; Intent's hook carrier wires only Intent's
body:
Routed from devbin#0078 on hv's ruling (2026-09-16, to devbin/vc in session), which chose between devbin, a devbin detector, and Intent: **Intent owns hook wiring.**

**The defect.** `.git/hooks/` is untracked in every git repository by construction. Intent already writes `.git/hooks` in every estate (`pre-commit.intent`) and runs its own guards from there. A project's OWN guards, wired by hand into `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, are lost on every fresh clone, and nothing prints to say so. The clone still runs Intent's guards, so its commits are gated -- by fewer guards than the project's own checkout -- and the difference cannot be seen from the clone.

**Measured at Lamplight (reported 2026-08-28, devbin#0035, instance 2).** Four project guards were hand-wired through `.git/hooks/pre-commit`. Their bodies are tracked in `bin/hooks/`, so only the wiring is lost, which makes the loss quieter rather than smaller. One guard, `whiteboard-inbox-guard`, vanishes outright. Every consumer that hand-wires hooks has the same gap.

**The ask.** Intent's hook carrier wires the project's own guards as well as its own, from a tracked declaration, so a fresh clone runs the same set as the original checkout. Failing that, it at least reports a declared guard that `.git/hooks` does not run. The shape is Intent's to choose. devbin's `precommit` builtin runs a gate and never wires a hook (devbin#0035, ruled the same day), so there is nothing on the devbin side to reconcile.


**CLOSED 2026-09-16, landed on vc's word at 0732b3bc8.** Intent takes the first shape the ask offers: a project declares its own guards in `intent/.config/config.json` as `"guards": [{"run": ["<tracked path>", "<arg>"], "when": "<path>"}]`, and Intent's hook runs them after its own roster. The declaration is tracked, so a fresh clone runs the same set. `run` is an argv never given to a shell. `when` is an optional path, and the guard is skipped as not applicable while nothing exists there. A declared guard whose body is missing, not executable or untracked, or a `guards` array that cannot be read, blocks the commit with a remedy. `--list-guards` gains a fifth column (`intent` or `project`), and `int hooks` reads all five. `Config` types the array, and `lang init` and `lang remove` keep it. The fallback half of the ask, reporting what `.git/hooks` runs that no declaration covers, is in `intent doctor` as advisories that are not counted. It reports an untracked chain line no guard declares, a guard both declared and hand-wired, and a tracked `.githooks` or `bin/hooks` `pre-commit` while `core.hooksPath` is unset (that setting lives in `.git/config`, so a clone loses it too). Documented in `intent/docs/pre-commit-hook.md` under Project guards. Adopting it at Lamplight and the other estates, Intent's own included, is a separate pass.
